article.intro: Good drum and bass names hit hard and fast: one sharp word, often with a k or an x where a c would be, an "A & B" duo, or an MC tag that cuts through a rewind. This **drum and bass name generator** makes producer and DJ names, duos and crews, MC names and EP titles.

sections.heading: Eight good drum and bass names
sections.content:
All eight came from the generator, across producers, duos, MCs and records:

  • Morfik: a stylised spelling, which is how a lot of DnB aliases stand out.
  • Strata: one hard, technical word, the neurofunk way.
  • Zeno & Kryo: two short aliases with an ampersand, the standard duo shape.
  • Kings of the Night Bus: a crew name for anyone who's left a rave at 6am.
  • MC Diction: an MC tag about the voice itself.
  • MC Riddla D: rhyme-speak spelling plus an initial, as MCs often have.
  • Rain on Concrete: a liquid-style EP title: wet streets and city lights.
  • Mass & Velocity: a physics title for something heavy and fast.

sections.heading: How drum and bass names itself
sections.content:
Drum and bass grew out of UK jungle in the early 1990s, built on chopped-up breakbeats. The most famous of them, the Amen break, comes from a six-second drum solo on "Amen, Brother", a 1969 B-side by The Winstons. From the start the scene ran on pirate radio, dubplates and MCs hyping the crowd, and the names still show it:

  • Producers and DJs pick one word that sounds like engineering or physics, and bend the spelling: Circuitry, Oxide, Synaptix.
  • Duos put two names either side of an ampersand: Alloy & Kinetic, Inertia & Radar.
  • MCs are "MC" plus a word about speed or lyrics, or a name with MC after it: MC Rapid, Static MC.
  • EPs are often just one word and "EP", or two track titles with a slash, the way a two-track release lists its A-side and B-side: Tremor / Tundra.

Each sub-genre leans its own way. Liquid names are soft and watery (Stay Liquid), while neurofunk names sound like lab equipment (Axon EP, Capacitor Theory).

sections.heading: Using a drum and bass name
sections.content:
• Make it readable at speed. Your name will scroll past on a stream and sit at the bottom of a line-up, so one word usually works best.
  • Don't overdo the spelling. One swapped letter makes a name yours; three makes it impossible to search for.
  • MCs, test it out loud. If the host can't shout it clearly over a drop, pick another.
  • Check it's free on Beatport, Discogs, SoundCloud and Spotify. DnB has a lot of one-word aliases already.

faqs.question: What are good drum and bass names?
faqs.answer: One sharp word with a technical feel, often with a stylised spelling: Morfik, Strata or Oxide. For a duo, put two of them either side of an ampersand, like Zeno & Kryo.

faqs.question: How do I pick an MC name for drum and bass?
faqs.answer: Keep it short and easy to shout: MC plus a word about your voice or speed, like MC Diction or MC Rapid. Choose MC name in the generator.

faqs.question: Is drum and bass the same as jungle?
faqs.answer: They're closely related. Jungle came first, in the early 1990s, and drum and bass grew out of it; the names in this generator suit both.
